ashtanga_limbs: Yama (Ethical Restraints: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya, Aparigraha)
Niyama (Self-Disciplines: Saucha, Santosha, Tapas, Svadhyaya, Ishvara Pranidhana)
Asana (Steady and Comfortable Posture: Sthira Sukham Asanam)

primary_alignment_cues: Ground evenly through all four corners of the standing foot.
Engage the standing quadriceps and lift the kneecap without hyperextending the joint.
Place the sole of the lifted foot on the inner thigh or inner calf; avoid placing the foot directly on the knee joint.
Abduct the bent knee outward while keeping the pelvis level and square to the front.
Draw the navel gently toward the spine to stabilize the lumbar spine.
Bring hands to Anjali Mudra (prayer posture) at the sternum or extend arms overhead with shoulders relaxed.
benefits: Strengthens ankles, calves, and inner thighs.
Improves neuromuscular balance, proprioception, and poise.
Stretches the groins, inner thighs, chest, and shoulders.
Develops sustained mental focus and concentration.
contraindications: Acute knee ligament injuries (place foot lower on the calf or keep toes touching the floor).
Severe vertigo or unmanaged inner ear disorders (practice near a wall for balance support).
Severe osteoarthritis of the hip joint.
variations: Tree pose with foot resting on a yoga block.
Tree pose with eyes closed for advanced proprioceptive training.

primary_alignment_cues: Stand with big toes touching or feet hip-width apart.
Root through the heel, ball of the foot, and outer edge.
Stack knees over ankles, hips over knees, and shoulders over hips.
Lengthen the tailbone down toward the heels while drawing the lower belly in.
Broaden across the collarbones and let the arms rest by the sides with palms forward.
benefits: Improves structural posture and spinal axial alignment.
Strengthens thighs, knees, and ankles.
Reduces flat feet symptoms and tones the pelvic floor.
contraindications: Headache or lightheadedness (widen stance).
Low blood pressure episodes.
variations: Urdhva Hastasana (Upward Salute with arms extended).
Tadasana with a yoga block between the inner thighs to reinforce adductor engagement.

primary_alignment_cues: Spread fingers wide, rooting through the index finger and thumb knuckles (Hasta Bandha).
Rotate the upper arms outward to create space around the cervical spine.
Send sitting bones high and back, lengthening from wrists to pelvis.
Maintain axial elongation in the spine before attempting to straighten the knees.
Descend heels toward the mat without collapsing the inner arches.
benefits: Decompresses the entire spinal column.
Strengthens shoulders, triceps, serratus anterior, and wrist flexors.
Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and Achilles tendons.
contraindications: Carpal tunnel syndrome (use forearm modification or incline blocks).
Late-stage pregnancy.
Severe uncontrolled hypertension.
variations: Bent-knee downward dog to prioritize lumbar elongation.
Dolphin pose (Pincha Mayurasana prep on forearms).

primary_alignment_cues: Front knee bent at a 90-degree angle directly stacked over the front ankle.
Back foot grounded at a 45-degree angle with the outer heel firmly pressed down.
Square both anterior superior iliac spines (hip points) toward the front edge of the mat.
Lift the arch of the rear foot and engage the rear quadriceps.
Elevate arms overhead, drawing the lower ribs inward to prevent excessive lumbar arching.
benefits: Strengthens quadriceps, gluteus medius, and calf musculature.
Lengthens the psoas major and hip flexors of the posterior leg.
Expands thoracic lung capacity.
contraindications: Recent spinal disk herniation (limit pelvic backbend).
Hypertension (keep hands on hips rather than overhead).
variations: High Lunge (Crescent Lunge with back heel lifted).
Hands in prayer position at chest center.

primary_alignment_cues: Front knee tracking in line with the second and third toes, stacked at 90 degrees.
Back foot parallel or slightly angled inward to the back edge of the mat.
Pelvis open toward the long side of the mat while maintaining front knee abduction.
Extend arms parallel to the floor at shoulder height, reaching actively through both fingertips.
Gaze steadily over the middle finger of the front hand (Drishti).
benefits: Strengthens lower extremity stabilizers and core endurance.
Deeply opens hips and stretches adductor muscles.
Fosters psychological resilience and grounded stability.
contraindications: Meniscus or knee collateral ligament pathology (shorten stance width).
Chronic shoulder impingement (keep arms lower than shoulder line).
variations: Warrior II with chair support under the front thigh.
Restricted arm elevation with hands at heart center.

primary_alignment_cues: Kneel on the floor with big toes touching and knees comfortably wide.
Sink hips back toward the heels.
Fold the torso forward between the thighs, resting forehead gently on the mat.
Extend arms forward with palms down or drape them back along the shins with palms up.
Breathe deeply into the posterior ribs and lumbar space.
benefits: Calms the central nervous system, shifting tone to parasympathetic dominance.
Gently opens hips, thighs, and ankles.
Relieves fatigue, stress, and mild lower back tension.
contraindications: Acute knee inflammation or recent knee surgery.
Diarrhea or acute digestive distress.
variations: Child's pose with a bolster beneath the torso.
Child's pose with folded blanket under knees or behind knee creases.

primary_alignment_cues: Lie prone with legs extended and the tops of the feet pressed firmly into the floor.
Position palms beneath shoulders with elbows hugged close to the ribcage.
Inhale and lift the chest off the floor using spinal extensor musculature rather than pushing through the arms.
Maintain broad clavicles and draw the shoulder blades down the back.
Keep the cervical spine neutral, avoiding hyper-extension of the neck.
benefits: Strengthens the erector spinae, latissimus dorsi, and gluteal muscles.
Increases spinal mobility and counters sedentary slouching.
Stimulates abdominal organs and opens the chest.
contraindications: Spondylolisthesis or severe spinal stenosis.
Carpal tunnel syndrome (use Sphinx pose on forearms).
Pregnancy.
variations: Salamba Bhujangasana (Sphinx Pose with forearms on the ground).
Baby Cobra without weight in hands.

primary_alignment_cues: Lie supine with knees bent and feet planted parallel, hip-width apart.
Heels positioned close to sitting bones, reachable with fingertips.
Press through all four corners of both feet and lift hips toward the ceiling.
Roll shoulder heads beneath the torso and interlace fingers along the mat.
Keep thighs parallel, avoiding outward splaying of the knees.
benefits: Strengthens gluteus maximus, hamstrings, and spinal extensors.
Opens the anterior chest, sternum, and anterior hip flexors.
Rejuvenates tired legs and calms cerebral overactivity.
contraindications: Acute cervical spine pathology (do not turn head while hips are elevated).
Third-trimester pregnancy.
variations: Supported Bridge with a yoga block placed horizontally under the sacrum.
One-legged bridge (Eka Pada Setu Bandhasana) for unilateral strength.

primary_alignment_cues: Lie completely flat on the back with legs extended and feet falling open naturally.
Place arms at a 30-degree angle from the torso with palms facing upward.
Allow the jaw, tongue, eyes, and brow to release all muscular tension.
Let the breath return to its natural, unforced autonomic rhythm.
Remain motionless and consciously present for 5 to 15 minutes.
benefits: Consolidates physiological benefits of the physical asana practice.
Reduces systemic cortisol levels and balances blood pressure.
Facilitates cellular recovery and deep psychological rejuvenation.
contraindications: Severe respiratory discomfort or acid reflux (elevate head and chest with a bolster).
Late-term pregnancy (lie in left lateral decubitus position).
variations: Savasana with a bolster beneath the knee popliteal fossa to relieve lumbar strain.
Weighted Savasana with a sandbag on the pelvis or eye pillow over the orbits.
